title: Legacy client parity: embeddings + rerank compatibility shim and cursor pagination semantics
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Summary:
We need to deliver a compatibility layer that makes Redwood's current embeddings and rerank endpoints behave identically (or predictably degradable) for legacy clients that expect older parameter names, error shapes, and pagination semantics. This ticket covers shaping request/response contracts, error code mapping, and a cursor-based pagination contract for rerank/embeddings that matches our compatibility promise to customers migrating from other APIs or earlier versions of our SDKs.

Scope / Goals:
- Provide a server-side compatibility shim that accepts legacy parameter names (batching hints, model aliases, 'limit' vs 'page_size') and maps them to the current API internally without changing primary APIs.
- Standardize embedding return structure and metadata keys so both new and legacy clients get deterministic vectors, length and dimension fields, and stable distance metric metadata.
- Harmonize rerank endpoint pagination: implement deterministic cursor semantics (opaque cursors) plus a backwards-compatible offset mode for clients that cannot support cursors.
- Define a canonical error taxonomy and mapping table so older SDKs see the error codes they expect (e.g., 400 -> INVALID_ARGUMENT, 429 -> RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, 500 -> INTERNAL), including a stable `error.code` string field and `retry_after` where applicable.
- Provide migration guidance, examples and test fixtures for SDK teams and customers.

Non-Goals:
- Do not change the primary modern API contract; the shim must sit behind a compatibility flag or accept legacy headers.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility shim accepts legacy params: 'limit', 'cursor', 'batch_size', 'model_alias' and translates them to current fields without user-facing schema changes.
Embeddings responses include: 'vector' (float list), 'dimension' (int as string), 'model' (string), and optional 'distance_metric' metadata in all compatibility responses.

Rerank endpoint supports opaque cursor strings that encode sort key + shard offset; cursor mode returns stable page boundaries and is the default for compatibility header. Offset mode remains available when client sends Legacy-Pagination: offset header.

Error responses include top-level fields: 'status_code' (HTTP), 'error.code' (stable string), 'error.message' (string), and optional 'retry_after' (seconds) where applicable; mapping table documented in Confluence.
Automated integration tests exist for: legacy request shapes, cursor round-trip determinism, error mapping for rate limits and validation failures, and vector shape consistency across batching modes.
SDK teams verify the shim by running compatibility test suite (pass rate >= 98%) and sign off in the linked PRs.
Compatibility mode can be toggled via header 'X-Redwood-Compat: legacy-v1' and will be documented in the API changelog.
No regression in core modern API performance beyond a 3% median latency increase when compatibility header is not present.
Telemetry emits feature flag usage metric and compatibility-mapping errors for 30 days after rollout.
Release notes, migration guide, and example curl + Node/Python snippets published before cutover date.
activity_log: 2026-03-10: Ticket created by Aisha Raman. Initial scoping and stakeholders (SDK, Runtime, Console) listed.
2026-03-11: Engineering sync - ENG-5021 assigned for kernel-level vector normalization checks. Agreed to use opaque base64 cursors for cursor mode. (Diego)

2026-03-12: PM/Design review: decided to expose 'distance_metric' in 'meta' object rather than top-level to avoid collision with existing client fields. Added to acceptance criteria. (Aisha, Priya S.)
2026-03-13: Security reviewed shim surface; concluded no additional secrets required but audit logging must include original legacy params. (Security)
2026-03-14: Draft API spec uploaded and linked; ENG asked for example payloads and e2e fixtures. Estimate finalized to 5 pts. (Diego)
